problem_series.thesis: The exact factorial-successor and carry normal forms, integral-channel and projection consumers, an unconditional finite denominator exclusion through 300000, and five quantified producer problems for the still-open factorial-denominator series.

The centred integer state and defect identity, absorption of a vanishing state, descent for the nonnegative case, and exclusion of the negative case when its magnitude is constant, periodic, or bounded, the last conditional on two assumed analytic inputs; unbounded negative excursions survive.

A standalone theorem-led account of the exact dyadic-section ranks, infinite-dimensionality, explicit denominator exclusion, finite Euler-sieve identities, and scoped method boundaries for the still-open totient constant.

The exact finite prime-gap summation by parts with its endpoint retained, the integral-shift criterion and its totient consequence for an abstract dyadic tail recurrence, and the free-carry telescoping identity that closes the periodicity route.

A standalone theorem-led account of finite-period noncollapse, settled support families, finite-change invariance, achievement-set geometry, and the precise surviving boundary for universal Erdős Problem 257.

The running least common multiple of a three-prime smooth prefix, its literal dyadic block digits and bounded radix, exact residue/coboundary carry forms, higher-rank block and observer obstructions, and the conditional reduction to a coprime reduced carry; actual carry divisibility and cofinal window escape remain open.

Newton-flow value decay and critical-value ray separation, exact translation-collision geometry and root retention, plus a precise diagnosis of the invalid local saddle block in a recent claimed spanning-tree proof; the global topology and metric gluing remain open.

The coordinatewise corridor and its impossibility at base three halves, exact primitive-normalisation and endpoint-jet obstructions, the 81/200 external height region with checked parameter specialisations, and precise saturated Hermite-Pade and Mahler-system questions.

prime_gap_unboundedness.source_statement: The gaps between consecutive primes are unbounded; the elementary factorial construction gives arbitrarily long prime-free intervals.
prime_gap_unboundedness.mapping: The local theorem uses the zero-based consecutive-prime gap sequence and proves that for every bound B some indexed gap exceeds B. This is the same unboundedness statement after the repository's indexing convention is unfolded.

prime_gap_unboundedness.logical_dependency: The Lean proof reconstructs an elementary argument locally; no external prime-gap theorem is imported as a proof dependency.

eventually_periodic_lambert.source_statement: For an eventually periodic sequence of nonnegative rational coefficients that is not eventually zero, the associated Lambert series at an integer base b at least 2 is irrational.
eventually_periodic_lambert.mapping: The local theorem formalises the nonnegative rational eventually-periodic coefficient case. Its coefficient, base, sign, and non-eventual-zero hypotheses are kept explicit; it does not claim the broader mixed-sign theorem.
eventually_periodic_lambert.historical_attribution: Luca and Tachiya, Irrationality of Lambert series associated with a periodic sequence (2014), with the later RIMS exposition used for statement comparison.
eventually_periodic_lambert.logical_dependency: The local Lean proof uses a separate periodic-divisor certificate route; the cited paper establishes attribution and source fidelity, not a kernel dependency.

known_irrational_supports.source_statement: Several structured support families for the Mersenne reciprocal subseries are known to give irrational sums, including full support and other classical or later special families.
known_irrational_supports.mapping: The review family is an aggregate disclosure. Each local theorem retains its own support predicate; the Comparator selects full support as the classical representative and pairwise-coprime support as a dedicated exact non-dilation representative.
known_irrational_supports.historical_attribution: Erdos (1948) for full support; Erdos (1968), Luca--Tachiya, and Tao--Teravainen for the specific additional families identified in the paper and prior-art ledger.
known_irrational_supports.logical_dependency: The full-support and pairwise-coprime Comparator theorems are proved locally in Lean. Other family rows have their stated local or cited proof boundaries; historical attribution is not an imported Lean dependency.

pairwise_coprime_support.source_statement: For every integer base b at least 2 and every infinite pairwise-coprime support A with summable reciprocal mass, the support-restricted Mersenne reciprocal series is irrational.
pairwise_coprime_support.mapping: The local theorem keeps the base, infinitude, pairwise-coprimality, and summable-reciprocal hypotheses explicit and concludes irrationality of erdosSupportSeries b A. At base 2 this is exactly the pairwise-coprime support subfamily of Erdős #257; it is a separate non-dilation representative from the full-support row.
pairwise_coprime_support.historical_attribution: Erdos (1968), as recorded in the repository's prior-art ledger and the #257 problem note.
pairwise_coprime_support.logical_dependency: The proof-bearing source supplies the adaptive CRT and weighted coefficient certificate argument locally; the cited source establishes historical attribution and statement fidelity, not an imported Lean dependency.

achievement_set_geometry.source_statement: Kakeya's strict-tail criterion places rapidly decreasing subsum sets in the Cantor-set regime; for the fixed-base Mersenne sequence, Kovač--Tao verify the strict-tail inequality and distinct subsums.
achievement_set_geometry.mapping: At base 2 the local development formalises compactness, perfection, total disconnectedness, nowhere density, and measure one. The strict-tail Cantor geometry aligns with the cited antecedents; the measure-one clause is locally derived and carries no novelty assertion.
achievement_set_geometry.historical_attribution: Kakeya (1914) for the strict-tail subsum-set criterion and Kovač--Tao (2025), Remark 4.1, for the fixed-base Mersenne antecedent.
achievement_set_geometry.logical_dependency: The topology and measure theorem are proved locally in Lean; the cited sources fix historical/source alignment and are not imported proof objects.

erdos_borwein_full_support.source_statement: For every integer b at least 2, the full-support Lambert--Mersenne series sum over n at least 1 of 1/(b^n-1) is irrational.
erdos_borwein_full_support.mapping: The local theorem uses Nat indexing with exponent k+1, which is exactly the source sum after reindexing n=k+1; the base assumption is the same integer condition b at least 2.
erdos_borwein_full_support.historical_attribution: Erdos, On arithmetical properties of Lambert series (1948), theorem on p. 63 as recorded in the repository's prior-art ledger.
erdos_borwein_full_support.logical_dependency: The theorem is independently represented and proved in Lean in this repository; the historical source is attribution and fidelity evidence, not an imported kernel dependency.

totient_kernel_rank.source_statement: Coons proved that Euler's totient sequence is not k-regular for every integer k at least 2, while Martin's affine-totient ordering theorem implies linear independence of every finite family of pairwise nonproportional positive-slope affine totient sections.
totient_kernel_rank.mapping: The dyadic Lean development gives an independent constructive finite-level basis and rank proof. Its full-kernel infinite-dimensionality corollary is kernel-checked here but is not an independent contribution: for integer-valued sequence modules it is equivalent to Coons's non-k-regularity result. The all-base Lean modules check the zero-channel identity, the exact composite-base scalar reduction, residue coordinates, index cardinality k^e+1, and unconditional spanning by the canonical family. Lean also checks the exact-rank conclusion under an explicit linear-independence hypothesis. Martin remains the external authority for that hypothesis, so the unconditional all-base basis and rank theorem remains a paper conclusion rather than a Lean theorem without assumptions.
totient_kernel_rank.historical_attribution: Coons for non-k-regularity of Euler's totient sequence; Martin for the positive-density affine ordering theorem from which the paper's finite-family independence step follows.
totient_kernel_rank.logical_dependency: The dyadic finite-level proof is local. In the all-base development, arithmetic reduction and canonical spanning are unconditional; exact rank is conditional on an explicit linear-independence hypothesis. The paper discharges that hypothesis using Martin externally, whose positive-density theorem is not formalised.

claims.statement: The prime-index dyadic series remains open in this release; the exact tail-shift equivalence, prime-gap unboundedness, and nonperiodicity do not supply the required cofinal escape for the actual prime gaps.

claims.label: Unbounded and non-eventually-periodic consecutive prime gaps
claims.statement: The consecutive-prime-gap sequence is unbounded and is not eventually periodic with any positive period. These coefficient facts do not by themselves imply irrationality of the prime-gap or prime-index dyadic series.

claims.label: Exact prime-gap dyadic irrationality equivalence
claims.statement: For a summable prime dyadic term and its discrete prime-gap difference, irrationality of the prime-index dyadic series is equivalent to irrationality of the prime-gap dyadic series; this transfers the open question without proving either side.

claims.label: Erdős #1041: short connections inside polynomial lemniscates
claims.statement: The global short-connection assertion remains open in this release; finite ray-separation and root-retention inputs do not establish the required topology and length bound.

claims.label: Finite Newton-flow ray separation and perturbation consumer
claims.statement: An explicit exponential-decay Newton connection can occur only when its endpoint values lie on the same positive ray; conversely, every finite injective complex family admits an arbitrarily small common translation making all values nonzero and all positive-ray arguments distinct. These are finite perturbative and conditional connection statements.

claims.label: Full-support Erdős–Borwein irrationality, every integer base b ≥ 2
claims.statement: For every integer b ≥ 2, the series ∑_{n≥1} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational (Erdős, 1948).

claims.label: The Erdős–Borwein constant E is irrational
claims.statement: E = ∑_{n≥1} 1/(2ⁿ − 1) is irrational, as the base-2 corollary of the full-support theorem.

claims.label: Named infinite-support irrationality families toward #257
claims.statement: For every base b ≥ 2, ∑_{n∈A} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational for factorial support, power-of-two support, multiples, pairwise-coprime supports with summable reciprocals, eventually-periodic supports, residue classes, and the odd numbers. Proved families, not the universal statement.

claims.label: Quotient-band channel breakpoint for factorial moments
claims.statement: For a finite integer coefficient family whose indices all lie in one quotient band k·d ≤ i_j < (k+1)·d, the factorial moment is exactly (d!)^k times the d-channel numerator. In the first band d ≤ i_j < 2d, channel cancellation forces the factorial moment to vanish; with all indices at least d and a nonzero moment, some index is therefore at least 2d.

claims.label: Finite least-positive-residue contradiction for #269
claims.statement: For a positive modulus C, a positive integer state c bounded by K cannot be congruent to x modulo C when the canonical least-positive representative of x is greater than K; the zero residue class is represented by C. The integer carry form and exact residue classifier are checked in Lean.

claims.label: Conditional cofinal-window extinction of bounded carries for #269
claims.statement: If the denominator-dependent cofinal local-window residue escape holds, then for every positive multiplier B coprime to 30 there is no positive integral sequence satisfying the exact cleared recurrence d_{n+1}=b_n d_n−B m_n together with the corresponding short bound. The same contradiction applies to an explicitly absorbed nonzero common-factor carry after exact cancellation. The bridge from the actual running-LCM series to this carry system and the cofinal escape remain open.

claims.label: Eventually-periodic nonnegative weighted Lambert irrationality
claims.statement: For every integer base b ≥ 2, an eventually-periodic nonnegative rational coefficient sequence with a positive value at a positive index in its periodic region has irrational series ∑ γ(a)/(b^a − 1). This includes eventually-periodic natural-number weights and indicator supports. Luca–Tachiya prove a broader periodic rational-coefficient theorem by different methods; no priority claim is made here.

claims.label: Periodic signed-weight irrational-or-terminating dichotomy
claims.statement: For every integer base b ≥ 2 and every periodic integer weight w, the signed series ∑ w(a)/(b^a − 1) is irrational or some power of b times its value is an integer. Excluding that terminating alternative implies irrationality. The terminating alternative is not excluded in general, so the full mixed-sign periodic-coefficient theorem is not claimed.

claims.label: Period-four signed residue-selection obstruction
claims.statement: For the period-four signed weight 1,0,−1,0, the associated signed divisor coefficient vanishes for every n congruent to 3 modulo 4. A whole arithmetic progression can therefore carry zero coefficient, so residue-blind selection cannot force a protected nonzero residue for every periodic signed weight.

claims.label: Conditional orthogonal-petal sunflower reduction
claims.statement: For a finite-core orthogonal-petal bouquet at base 2, the exact uniform tail-selection predicate implies a forced-carry certificate supply and hence irrationality of the associated support series. Lean formalises the carry conversion and an explicit infinite alternating-core, squared-prime-petal bouquet whose elements have three prime factors with multiplicity. The tail-selection predicate itself is not proved, so this does not add an unconditional #257 support family.

claims.label: Composite dilation defect identity
claims.statement: For every positive support element a and positive x, the divisor-count coefficient at a·x is the coefficient at x, plus the distinguished new divisor when a does not divide x, plus an exact finite composite-dilation defect. For a finite-core orthogonal-petal bouquet, the ray defect is bounded by the finite exceptional-frame cardinality plus the petal-support divisor count. This local identity supplies no correlation estimate, tail selector, or irrationality theorem.

claims.label: Mixed prime-power support-layer identity
claims.statement: Exact p-adic and q-adic coefficient-layer operators commute. For distinct primes and a residual argument coprime to their product, the two-layer operator on the support coefficient equals the iterated exact-prime-power pullback. The checked singleton {12} fixture has mixed (2²,3) layer value one at residual argument one. This is finite coefficient algebra only, with no decimation transport, bounded-Ω endpoint, or irrationality theorem.

claims.label: Dyadic-prefix, block-safety, and primitive-overshoot interfaces
claims.statement: Inside a hypothetical dyadic-rational support value, a reduced finite positive prefix transports exactly to a residual rational support value and wrap-ratio certificate. For the half-greedy orbit, reduced and raw margins, three-depth take-run excess, primitive-lattice cap violation, support-coefficient tail gaps, and gcd-scaled predecessor overshoot are connected by exact identities and equivalences; cofinal supplies of the named witnesses imply that 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. Checked fixtures show that safe brackets with numerator monotonicity and a factor-11 predecessor rule are not inductive. No cofinal witness supply is proved, so neither half-membership nor universal Erdős #257 follows.

claims.label: Half-trapping reverse-carry interface
claims.statement: Scalar-relation-invariant rational-linear channels have no nontrivial square determinant at any rank. Separately, a common coefficient word with a 1/0 seam and a common following overlap forces the terminal reverse-carry difference to be a power of two times an odd integer; a common nonnegative real carry bound yields the corresponding dyadic spacing inequality. The module neither supplies reverse-carry presentations nor a predecessor overlap, so it is not a greedy separation or irrationality theorem.

claims.label: Half-carry reachability and compactness
claims.statement: At an unresolved even seam, the scalar transition reaches exactly every integer terminal carry other than the one value 2*δ-c. If canonical seam coordinates are supplied at every sufficiently large even depth, then admissible finite half-carry words occur cofinally; compactness yields an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2. The canonical seam-supply hypothesis is not proved.

claims.label: Cofinal square-root-strip return closure
claims.statement: The binary-scaled uncentred greedy half carry is antitone, and the square-root strip envelope divided by 2^N tends to zero. Therefore cofinal returns of the canonical greedy carry to that strip force the scaled carry to tend to zero and yield membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. The cofinal return hypothesis is not proved.

claims.label: Terminal-only cofinal square-root-strip closure
claims.statement: A normalized finite word with terminal half carry in the square-root strip has support-series value within (4M+12)/2^M of 1/2. Thus cofinally many such terminal-only witnesses, with neither coherent histories nor earlier-row bounds, force 1/2 into the Mersenne achievement set and yield an infinite support with support-series value 1/2. The cofinal terminal-witness supply is not proved.

claims.label: Scaled terminal-vanishing closure
claims.statement: A normalized sequence of finite terminal words whose depths tend to infinity and whose terminal carries divided by the corresponding powers of 2 tend to zero has support-series values converging to 1/2. Closedness of the Mersenne achievement set then gives membership of 1/2 and an infinite support with that value. The prior cofinal square-root-strip condition maps into this weaker socket, but no scaled-vanishing sequence is constructed.

claims.label: Finite shadows of the half cylinder
claims.statement: For an admissible depth-N half-carry word with support A, terminal carry K_N, and future tail T_N, the residual is exactly 1/2 - X_A = (K_N - T_N)/2^N. At a first even seam the sole missing carry is H = 2 delta - c, so the integer strip [1,B] is fully reachable exactly when H lies outside it. The rank-three fixture A = {2,3} has residual 1/42 < 1/32 but its depth-six strip [1,8] contains H = 3, so raw dyadic safety does not force seam escape. The sole conditional membership input is the unproved governed frozen-margin producer, which requires future coefficient rows to cover the centred carry within J <= k+1 after every skipped rank k+1.

claims.label: Fixed-coefficient rewind contraction
claims.statement: For coefficient c, the canonical inverse parent is T_c(k) = ceil((k+c)/2). For a length-L coefficient list with accumulated offset O, the iterated rewind is R(k) = floor((k+O)/2^L), with phase theta = (1+O) mod 2^L. If 1 <= B <= 2^L, all targets in [1,B] have one ancestor exactly when theta + B - 1 < 2^L; otherwise the endpoint ancestors differ by one and every target maps to one of that adjacent pair. The width bound does not exclude the seam-pair alternative or prove half-membership.

claims.label: Selected half-carry windows
claims.statement: A selected half-carry window at depth N and radius R assigns every k in [1,R] an admissible Boolean word of depth N whose terminal carry is k. If such windows exist at every sufficiently large depth with R >= 1, their k = 1 representatives give cofinal finite admissibility; compactness then yields an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2. The unproved object-level input is a coherent one-row history: either all representatives agree on membership of every divisor of N+1, making their next coefficient common, or the adjacent outcome realizes the canonical one-hole seam. The module supplies no such cofinal history.

claims.label: Realized rewind phase identity
claims.statement: For a realized carry-one fixed-coefficient history, list the suffix bits newest row first and let X be their binary numeral, so the newest bit has weight 2^0. If D = 2^L, the rewind phase is exactly theta = D - 1 - X. The interval [1,B] rewinds to one ancestor exactly when B - 1 <= X; equivalently, for the frozen-prefix carry Z = 1 + X, exactly when B <= Z. No theorem proves either coverage inequality at all sufficiently large depths.

claims.label: Localized protected seam compactness
claims.statement: At depth M, realized localized seam means only the forward implication: every seam-reachable carry k in [3,27] is the terminal carry of an admissible finite word. The seam's unique hole is H = 2 delta - c, so choosing k = 4 when H = 3 and k = 3 otherwise supplies one admissible word. If such realizations occur cofinally, then cofinal admissibility and an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2 follow. The cofinal realization supply is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

claims.label: Mixed cofinal half-carry fan-in
claims.statement: For every N, suppose there is M >= N carrying either a selected protected half-carry window or a localized realized one-hole seam. The window branch chooses carry 1; the seam branch chooses 4 when its unique hole is 3 and 3 otherwise. Either branch supplies one admissible finite word, and the branches may alternate with N. Hence cofinal admissibility and, by compactness, an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2 follow. This mixed cofinal hypothesis is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

claims.label: Integer-greedy first-wrap reduction
claims.statement: For every s >= 3, let C_s = 2^(2s-1) - 2^s, let B_s = 2 floor(sqrt(2s)) + 4, and let r_s be the remainder obtained by greedily subtracting each descending truncated seam weight from C_s whenever possible. Each weight exceeds its complete tail by at least 2^(s+1) > B_s. Hence a positive subset-sum defect at most B_s exists exactly when 1 <= r_s <= B_s. The downstream skipped-seam escape hypothesis requires B_s < r_s at every genuine skipped rank. That hypothesis is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

claims.label: Concrete finite seam adapter
claims.statement: Concrete finite seam words realize the abstract adjacent-cut recurrence, and the next seam word agrees with the integer-greedy choice. This implements the finite recurrence but does not establish the unbounded remainder estimate.

claims.label: Fatal-gap and eventual-right seam classification
claims.statement: The concrete seam is eventually right when some S >= 5 makes every later seam word append true. A finite prefix u through rank d is a fatal half gap when V(u) + T_(d+1) < 1/2 < V(u) + w_(d+1), which makes every continuation miss 1/2. Eventual rightness is equivalent to the existence of such a gap, to nonmembership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set, and to a final skipped exponent in the real greedy orbit. This exact classification does not decide which branch holds.

claims.label: Canonical quotient-greedy and scaled-remainder frontier at 1/21
claims.statement: Membership of 1/21 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent both to excluding one explicit fatal/cofinite/aligned branch and to cofinally bounded scaled actual greedy remainders. Every closed Boolean quotient row is the deterministic quotient-greedy row; any unbounded sequence of canonical rows with remainder at most 2^R gives membership. On the complementary fatal branch the remainder is eventually strictly supercapacity, the boundary rank is always selected, and support and remainder follow one exact affine recurrence. A final skipped exponent also forces a structured one-sided approximation to the Erdős–Borwein constant with exact denominator-order constraints. These results isolate permanent affine supercapacity as the surviving late regime; they do not contradict it or prove 1/21 membership.

claims.label: Upper and first middle producers cannot feed an all-right tail
claims.statement: At a putative last false rank D ≥ 13, the upper producer is impossible unconditionally. On the middle branch, let u be the finite support below D and B_D = u union {n : n > D} the lazy support that skips D and selects every later rank. Its value is V(u) + T_D < 1/2, while the exact carry swap sends transition carry C_D to centred carry C_D + 3 at row 2D+1. Thus C_D = -3 gives centred carry zero; the next coefficient rows have at least one and two forced divisors and make the carry negative by row 2D+3, contradicting finite-level nonnegativity below 1/2. This removes the upper branch and one middle cell, not the right-tail branch or the remaining cells -2 and -1.

claims.label: Rank-26 phase sieve for the final middle -2 cell
claims.statement: For every seam row s ≥ 27, the greedy decisions through rank 26 select exactly ranks 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 20, 21, and 26. Consequently, in a hypothetical final middle -2 cell at rank D ≥ 27 followed by an all-right suffix, D mod 21 lies in {11, 14, 17, 20}, D mod 10 is not 8, the mod-10 class 7 cannot pair with the mod-21 class 11, D mod 13 is not 11, and the mod-13 class 10 cannot pair with the mod-21 class 11. Exactly 412 of the 2730 joint residue classes survive. This is a finite necessary condition, not an exclusion; even a later survivor density tending to zero would not suffice without finite extinction or an Archimedean contradiction. The -1 and right-tail branches remain open.

claims.label: Last-producer tail-escape reduction
claims.statement: If every actual middle transition at D ≥ 13 other than the discharged cell C_D = -3 satisfies Theta_D < C_D, then an eventual right seam is impossible and 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. Since Theta_D ≥ 0, this leaves two open inputs: exclude C_D = -2,-1 and prove Theta_D < C_D at every remaining transition with C_D ≥ 0. A square-root producer lower bound is a separate sufficient hypothesis. None of these arithmetic inputs is proved.

claims.label: Finite-prefix middle-producer cardinality reduction
claims.statement: Put g_D = #G_D. The augmented finite support A_D = G_D union {D} has g_D + 1 elements, so its complete future divisor-incidence tail satisfies Theta_D ≤ g_D + 1. Since C_D = 4 R_(D,D) - P_D - 4, the inequality g_D + P_D + 5 < 4 R_(D,D) is exactly g_D + 1 < C_D; required at every late middle transition, it excludes the negative cells and proves tail dominance, hence half-membership. The stronger row-scale hypothesis R_(D,D) ≥ D also suffices. Neither hypothesis is proved.

claims.label: Upper-reset dyadic-band certificates through row 30
claims.bounded_domain: Upper transitions at every row 13 <= d <= 30 and every band index j <= d; no row d > 30 is checked.
claims.statement: At an upper transition G_(d+1) = H_d, put Q_d = 4 O_d + A_d from the upper overshoot and divisor pulse and B_(d,j) = 2^(d-j+1). For every 13 <= d <= 30 and j <= d, Lean proves B_(d,j) < Q_d or Q_d + 2(d+j) <= B_(d,j), equivalently avoidance of Q_d <= B_(d,j) < Q_d + 2(d+j). For fixed d, one exact successor remainder R_(d+1,d+1) certifies every j. This is bounded evidence and proves no global upper-reset band-escape hypothesis.

claims.label: Positive half-membership classification in seam coordinates
claims.statement: Membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent to false successor terminal bits beyond every bound, to a cofinal sequence of such bits, and to a cofinal integer-seam sequence whose skipped ranks tend to infinity. These equivalences do not establish that any positive producer exists.

claims.label: Largest skipped-rank gap and successor propagation
claims.statement: At row s, let d be the largest skipped rank, u the selected prefix below d, L the integer weight of u together with the filled suffix above d, and U the weight obtained by replacing that suffix with d. In the late range d > 2s/3, equivalently 2s < 3d, Lean proves 3L + (3*2^(s+1) + 2*4^(s-d) + 4) = 3U. Upper or middle successors make the new terminal rank s the largest skip, while right successors preserve d. The global statement forcing an upper or middle step when 2(s+1) < 3d first fails is not proved.

claims.label: Boundary-pulse normalization at the largest-skip crossing
claims.statement: The row-s pulse of a selected rank e contributes two when e divides 2s+1 and one when e divides 2s+2. For a largest skip d with 2s < 3d, every filled suffix rank d < e < s divides neither index, so the word pulse is exactly the selected-prefix pulse below d. At the first crossing 2s < 3d <= 2(s+1), either 3d = 2s+1 with pulse two or 3d = 2s+2 with pulse one. The transition-carry estimate that would use these exact counts is not proved.

claims.label: Largest-skip induction from a quantified first-crossing hypothesis
claims.statement: Assume that for every s >= 14 and largest skip d with 2s < 3d, either 2(s+1) < 3d or the transition to row s+1 is upper or middle. Lean checks the base s = 14, d = 13 with 28 < 39. Under the hypothesis, induction gives a largest skip beyond two thirds at every row s >= 14; these skipped ranks tend to infinity, so 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. The universal next-row hypothesis is not proved.

claims.label: Fixed-tail survival equivalence at every actual skip
claims.statement: Writing r_M(1/2) for the residual after ranks through M and T_M for the complete tail after M, an actual skip M is final exactly when T_M < r_M(1/2). Negating the existence of a final skip yields r_M(1/2) <= T_M at every actual skip; together with the no-final-skip classification, this is equivalent to membership of 1/2. The required inequalities along the actual greedy orbit are not proved.

claims.label: Exact producer-carry residual and sign criteria
claims.statement: For A contained in {2,...,d}, let f_A(n) count support divisors, let C_(A,d) be the affine integer state after 2d+1 updates from 1, and let Theta_(A,d) be the complete scaled coefficient tail after depth 2d+2. Then 1/2 - X_A = 2^(-(2d+2))(C_(A,d) - Theta_(A,d)). Hence C_(A,d) > Theta_(A,d) iff X_A < 1/2 and C_(A,d) < Theta_(A,d) iff X_A > 1/2; a negative carry is sufficient for the latter because the tail is nonnegative, and carry at most -8 gives a full Mersenne-gap margin. No occurrence theorem for these carries is proved.

claims.label: Exact quarter-band failure cells for adjacent seam cuts
claims.statement: At row s put H = 2^(s-1), and let R, U, R', p^-, p^+ be the adjacent cut's remainder, overshoot, next remainder, below pulse, and above pulse. On the non-carry middle branch, failure R' >= 8H is equivalent to the unique cell R = H+k with p^- <= 4k < p^-+4. On the terminal-reset branch, failure is equivalent to R = 3H+k with p^-+4 <= 4k and 4k+16H < 4(R+U)+p^+. These are exact failure classifications, not an avoidance theorem for the concrete seam orbit.

claims.label: Exact right-branch window and reset-deficit escape law
claims.statement: Write R_s for the final integer-greedy remainder and p_s^- for the below pulse. At a largest skip d with 2s < 3d, a right branch forces 2^(s+1)+4 <= 4R_s and 12R_s+3*2^(s+1) < 4*(3*2^(s+1)+2*4^(s-d)+4)+6(s-2), and it satisfies R_(s+1)+2^(s+1)+p_s^-+4 = 4R_s. If R_s <= 2^s and delta_s = 2^s-R_s, every further right step gives delta_(s+1) >= 4 delta_s while the reference scale doubles; hence 2^s <= 2^k delta_s forces an upper-or-middle row t in [s,s+k]. The global anti-concentration needed to exclude the pinned interval along the actual orbit is not proved.

claims.label: Exact seam-hole to producer-carry alignment identity
claims.statement: Let P omit s, put A = P union {s}, and let delta be the half-carry of A at row 2s-2. Define the first-wrap hole H = 2 delta - f_P(2s) and paired incidence pulse Pi = 2 f_A(2s+1) + f_A(2s+2). Then the producer carry is exactly C(A,s) = 4(H-1) - Pi. This aligns the seam and producer coordinates but supplies no sign, size, or occurrence estimate.

claims.label: Computed depth-18 selected half-carry window base
claims.bounded_domain: The 12 terminal carries in the half strip at depth 18, together with their common depth-13 restriction and the next-row divisor-agreement certificate.
claims.statement: A kernel-reflected Boolean table supplies a selected half-carry window at depth 18 for every terminal carry in the half strip [1,12]. The representatives share a common depth-13 restriction, yielding the first next-row divisor-agreement certificate. This is a finite base and does not construct selected windows at unbounded depths.

claims.label: Operational bridge from rewind seams to protected next-row seams
claims.statement: Let W = (a^h)_(1 <= h <= R) be a selected depth-N window whose targets rewind to two adjacent base words at depth M. If D and phi are the rewind denominator and phase, delta = D-phi, M <= N, (N+1)/2 <= M, R <= D, and the adjacent base words have row-(N+1) coefficients c+1 and c, then f_(a^h)(N+1) equals c+1 for h <= delta and c for h > delta. If 27 <= S <= 2 floor(sqrt(N+1))+4 and S+c+1 <= 2R, the profile realizes a protected one-hole seam at row N+1. The rewind provenance, seam pair, coefficient drop, strip, and buffer are inputs. For a full half-strip window the divisor bound supplies the buffer, but the coefficient drop remains unproved.

claims.label: Conditional suffix-cylinder feedback and child-gap recurrence
claims.statement: For the depth-18 selected window, the common depth-13 prefix and suffix numeral satisfy ν + k = 17. Under a common next coefficient C the endpoint obeys E' = 2E - C. At a feedback row the full cylinder either advances or leaves one carry gap [g_-,g_+]. If the lower and upper families have coefficients C_- and C_+ and satisfy the explicit positivity, ordering, strip, and buffer inequalities, the next gap is exactly [2g_- - C_- - 1, 2g_+ - C_+]. Cutoff promotion appends forced bits 0 and 1 and preserves consecutive prefixes. A swallowed two-row update forces the sharp quarter-band bound B <= 4(g_+ - g_- + 1) + 2. Cofinal full stages would produce an infinite support of value 1/2, but no such cofinal family or uniform coefficient inequalities are proved.

claims.label: Verified finite suffix-cylinder stages through depth 52
claims.bounded_domain: Every depth from 18 through 29, plus explicit full stages at depths 51 and 52; depth 29 has common suffix cylinders at cutoffs 14 through 25 but not 26.
claims.statement: A common depth-13 prefix supports full selected windows at every depth 18 through 27, and the threshold continuation reaches depth 29 while covering the protected strip. At depth 29, cutoffs 14 through 25 remain common and cutoff 26 does not. A separate exact recurrence reaches depth 51 with endpoint 51,327,745 beyond the next head threshold, and the promoted depth-52 successor supplies a terminal-strip witness. These are finite stages, not an unbounded induction.

claims.label: Half-divisor unit coefficient drop at the feedback row
claims.statement: At the doubled feedback row, switching only the terminal half-divisor bit from false to true changes the support coefficient from C to C+1 and, under K' = 2K-C, drops the successor carry by exactly one. The same identity holds for any explicitly identified adjacent boundary pair, and the rewind adapter transfers such a shared-cutoff pair to the next protected seam while retaining the unit-drop witness. This does not construct such pairs globally.

claims.label: Finite rewind boundary-pair obstruction
claims.statement: A concrete depth-26 selected two-word window has a depth-27 explicit rewind step with history [1], a width-two numerical seam, and the doubled-row identity, but no depth-13 half-divisor boundary-pair witness. Therefore scalar one-row seam data alone does not entail the structural boundary predicate required by the cofinal consumer.

claims.label: Concrete adjacent-cut producer-carry coordinates
claims.statement: For every adjacent cut at rank s ≥ 5, the below and above words are the neighbouring subset sums bracketing the target; their remainder and overshoot are the unsigned distances, and their pulses are the paired divisor-incidence contributions of the next two rows. After adjoining terminal rank s, the below producer carry is 4 times the remainder minus the below pulse minus 4, while the above producer carry is the negative of 4 times the overshoot plus the above pulse plus 4. Hence the upper carry is negative and the middle sign depends on the remainder-pulse competition. These exact identities supply no uniform exponential lower bound, sign persistence at unbounded ranks, or universal escape argument.

claims.label: The Mersenne–Lambert ladder identities
claims.statement: L(μ) = 1/2, L(φ) = 2, L(φ*μ) = S, and the Möbius-square lens S = 1/2 + ∑ μ(d)/(2^d − 1)², placing the open constant one convolution from the machine-checked irrational E.

claims.label: Fair-coin coprimality form of the totient constant
claims.statement: For independent fair-coin geometric waiting times X and Y on the positive integers, S = 1/2 + P(gcd(X,Y)=1), where the probability is the visible coprime-pair series. That probability has no rational representation with denominator at most 39819823323350687661677887437915526. This is an exact reformulation and quantitative corollary; irrationality remains open.

claims.label: Squared-Lambert identities for divisor count and the first gcd moment
claims.statement: The squared-Mersenne Lambert series with weight 1 equals the base-1/2 series of sigma(n)-tau(n), and the series with weight phi equals the base-1/2 series of P(n)-n, where P is Pillai's gcd-sum function. These are the exact divisor-count and first-moment identities for the fair-coin gcd law; the separately cited irrationality of the constant-weight value is not claimed as formalised here.

claims.label: Reduced-direction normalization and Stern–Brocot cylinder law
claims.statement: The Mersenne weights of positive reduced slopes sum exactly to one. At every positive Stern–Brocot node (a,b), the cylinder mass 1/((2^a-1)(2^b-1)) splits into its stop mass and two child cylinders; the depth-d unfolding has error between zero and (2/3)^d times the cylinder mass and converges to the closed form.

claims.label: Fibonacci and continuant stability of Stern–Brocot runs
claims.statement: A Stern–Brocot word with r nonempty alternating runs has height at least F_(r+3), with equality on the all-unit run spine. Writing each run length as 1+e_i gives an exact multiaffine continuant-defect expansion, the sharp global gain F_(r+1) sum e_i, and exact one-site coefficient F_(i+2)F_(r-i+1). Under the gcd-one weight 2^-(a+b), the first induced run layer has mass 1/2, while the natural denominator-bookkeeping exponent is exactly F_(r+3)-2. These are source-level combinatorial and arithmetic facts; no analytic denominator survival or irrationality conclusion is claimed.

claims.label: Primitive Euler-coordinate finite-jet obstruction
claims.statement: For the primitive-conductor weight A = φ*μ, every positive index clearing the normalized coordinates A(n)/n through horizon N is divisible by the two-tier primorial: 4 at the prime 2 once N ≥ 4, p² for odd p with p² ≤ N, and p otherwise. Hence no fixed positive index clears all normalized coordinates. This is a finite Euler/Witt-coordinate obstruction only; it gives no irrationality criterion for S.

claims.label: Prime-power reduced-denominator unit-gap ceiling
claims.statement: For the reduced-denominator unit-gap predicate at an odd prime power p^e, the candidate interval is empty or has exactly one candidate divisible by p; in particular its count is at most one. The exact row (u,N,K) = (3,3,5) satisfies the unit-gap predicate while the corresponding ordinary empty-gap inequality fails. This is a finite certificate-level strengthening, not an unbounded supply theorem or an irrationality criterion for S.

claims.label: Finite Mersenne tail-atom determinant boundary
claims.statement: A periodic Mersenne tail atom has the exact doubling-and-wrap carry law. For any finite atom matrix, clearing the product of its column Mersenne denominators yields the integral numerator determinant; a nonzero cleared weighted minor therefore has absolute value at least one. This is a finite-denominator boundary for an atom-minor route, not an irrationality criterion for S.

claims.label: Möbius-sign support one-half no-go
claims.statement: The Boolean support selected by the negative Möbius values has sum 1/2 plus the positive Möbius tail and is therefore at least 1/2 + 1/63. This closes the sign-truncation route to the target value 1/2; it does not exclude another infinite Boolean support with that value.

claims.label: Totient carry anti-compression
claims.statement: If the binary totient coefficient series were rational, one positive-multiplier tempered integral carry would have uniformly eventually-periodic dyadic sections modulo its multiplier while retaining canonical carry-section span dimension at least 2^e − 1 for every e. No finite-rank bound for every rationality-supplied carry is proved, so this quotient-periodicity/anti-compression conjunction is a necessary consequence rather than an irrationality criterion for S.

claims.label: Unconditional denominator exclusion for the totient constant
claims.statement: S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ is not equal to p/q for any integer p and any 1 ≤ q ≤ 79 639 646 646 701 375 323 355 774 875 831 053 (≈ 7.96 × 10³⁴). A lower bound on any rational representation, not a proof of irrationality.

claims.label: Exact reduction of #249 to finite decidable certificates
claims.statement: S is irrational if and only if certified non-integrality witnesses occur at unbounded parameters. The pointwise completeness theorem and the diagonal supply theorem together show that an unbounded lcm-diagonal supply is equivalent as well. Producing that supply remains open.

claims.label: Certificate completeness
claims.statement: At fixed parameters, a certified kill exists exactly when the corresponding tail difference is non-integral. At every positive shift, integrality of one tail difference forces S to be rational; thus irrationality is equivalent to pointwise non-integrality, and to pointwise finite certificates.

claims.label: Initial certified-kill segment and generated certificates
claims.statement: Kernel-checked certified kills for the listed small periods, every lcm-diagonal scale t ≤ 82, and the finite certificate shards. The historical 28 explicit deposits through t = 64 form a strict subset of this contiguous finite band.
claims.bounded_domain: The explicitly listed small periods; every natural lcm-diagonal scale t with t ≤ 82; and the parameters encoded by the finite certificate shards. No certificate at t = 83 and no unbounded or cofinal supply is claimed.

claims.label: Exact full-target reduction on the lcm diagonal
claims.statement: At each lcm-diagonal scale, integrality is equivalent to a foreign-defect term landing in an explicit full-target interval. Globally, S is irrational if and only if the full target is avoided at arbitrarily large diagonal scales; that cofinal avoidance is not proved.

claims.label: Fresh-loss projection and suffix-supply reduction
claims.statement: The fresh-loss residue certificate is exactly an integer projection inequality, and such a projection forces full-target avoidance. An unbounded projection supply—or the stronger adjacent-suffix gap supplies formalised here—implies irrationality; no unbounded supply is asserted.

claims.label: T64 diagonal-pincer primality closure
claims.bounded_domain: The generated Lucas primality dependencies required by the diagonal-pincer certificate family through t = 64.
claims.statement: A generated proof-producing Lucas-certificate module supplies the primality dependencies for the t=47,49,53,59,61,64 diagonal-pincer certificates. This is finite certificate infrastructure; it neither supplies an unbounded certificate family nor proves irrationality.

claims.label: T64 diagonal-pincer endpoint certificate
claims.statement: Lean checks the diagonal-pincer certified kill at t = 64 using the committed T64 Lucas-primality closure. This is one finite certificate and does not assert an unbounded certificate supply or irrationality.

claims.label: Fresh-prime endpoint-deficit decomposition
claims.statement: At each positive height, every old-prime endpoint mass dominates the actual totient. The diagonal increment and literal foreign channel split exactly into the old Möbius increment and lower-minus-upper endpoint fresh deficits. The second and five-point curvature operators retain this split, and the nonnegative deficits bound the exact adverse weighted loss from the old-prime curvature margins. No cofinal deficit bound or irrationality conclusion is proved.

claims.label: Flexible three-rank odd-window reduction
claims.statement: At an analytically admissible odd power-of-two rank, centrality in any one of the canonical odd rank or its next two base-four successors supplies the existing adjacent-suffix gap interface and hence irrationality. The remaining assertion is a cofinal three-rank band supply; no such supply is proved.

claims.label: Affine three-scale frontier for the flexible odd window
claims.statement: Under the stated short-correction bounds, the three half-word central-band predicates are exactly a three-scale affine escape disjunction. A uniform correction envelope alone cannot force that escape, as a zero-start affine orbit remains inside every scaled edge tube. Thus arithmetic state-correction correlation remains required.

claims.label: Exact power-of-two one-bit lift
claims.statement: Given agreement modulo 2^k, agreement modulo 2^(k+1) is exactly evenness of the signed quotient after division by 2^k; failure gives the unique offset class. In particular, a signed difference 16*c agrees modulo 32 exactly when c is even. Under the stated correction and margin budget, the centered signed-margin socket is exactly failure of this next lift. This provides a finite fifth-bit interface and does not supply cofactor parity at unbounded scales.

claims.label: Parity obstruction for the reduced margin socket
claims.statement: For every positive even modulus and every radius in the stated nontrivial range, each parity class contains both a reduced-margin-socket hit and a miss. The same holds for a positive power-of-two modulus. Thus quotient parity alone cannot decide the reduced signed-margin socket. No t = 827 numeral or signed-margin certificate is asserted.

claims.label: Canonical strict-jump slack reduction
claims.statement: The two canonical adjacent-suffix central-band inequalities are equivalent to nonnegativity of one explicit integer slack. Cofinal nonnegative slack at strict lcm jumps implies irrationality of the totient constant; that cofinal sign statement remains open.

claims.label: Sharp squared-Mersenne diagonal enclosure
claims.statement: The scaled diagonal tail difference is written as an explicit Lambert-projected centre plus a signed squared-Mersenne tail, with a sharp symmetric bound and a checked separation criterion for missing the full target.

claims.label: Finite foreign-residue projection reduction
claims.statement: The finite Möbius residue diagonal splits exactly into projected foreign and divisor channels, and every finite stable tail window has a closed geometric bound. If an analytic kernel/complement bridge controls the actual foreign defect by that bound and the projection is separated from every integer, then the full target is missed. The analytic bridge and any unbounded separated-projection supply are not proved.

claims.label: Exact Mersenne-shadow denominator and survivor bounds
claims.statement: The reduced denominator of the lcm-height scaled Möbius shadow is computed exactly at every height, and for t ≥ 5 an explicit upper-half Mersenne product both divides it and supplies a quantitative lower bound.

claims.label: Scalar-localisation height obstruction
claims.statement: If H divides the reduced denominator of a rational x and the reduced denominator of c·x divides H for an integer c, then the complementary factor x.den/H divides |c|. Scalar localisation transfers, rather than discards, that denominator information; this local obstruction is not an irrationality criterion.

claims.label: Square-CRT correction suppression
claims.statement: For every finite family of distinct primes and prescribed anchors, a bounded simultaneous square-CRT base removes the prime-dilation correction at every admissible finite shift. Checked clean cubes can have vanishing coefficients and can also have a nonzero coefficient; this finite mechanism supplies neither an unbounded certificate family nor an irrationality criterion for the totient constant.

claims.label: Signed dyadic-moment algebra
claims.statement: A rectangular determinant expansion over all maps and a unique-largest-dyadic-exponent parity lemma are formalised. The latter makes a cleared finite dyadic sum odd, hence nonzero, when its selected numerator is odd and its exponent is strictly largest. This is finite algebraic substrate only: it proves neither non-vanishing of the actual totient Hankel determinants nor an irrationality criterion.

claims.label: Explicit basis of the dyadic totient kernel span
claims.statement: Lean constructs an explicit odd-core-indexed basis of the rational span of the full dyadic totient kernel, with exact span equality and linear independence. This is an independent constructive proof route; its infinite-dimensionality consequence is not an independent contribution because Coons's non-2-regularity theorem already implies it.

claims.label: Dyadic totient-kernel finite-level rank
claims.statement: For every e, a CRT–Dirichlet construction produces a separated nonzero evaluation minor for the canonical dyadic totient-kernel family, which is linearly independent with exact span dimension 2^e + 1. The same Lean development proves that the full dyadic kernel span is not finite-dimensional, but that corollary is not an independent contribution: it is equivalent, for this integer-valued sequence module, to Coons's non-2-regularity theorem. Even residues reduce to odd-core channels, and the compressed-adjoint boundary remains available. These coefficient-side theorems do not prove that S is irrational.

claims.label: All-base totient-kernel reduction, spanning, and conditional rank
claims.statement: For every integer base k at least 2, Lean checks the zero-residue scaling identity, the exact nonzero scalar used in composite-base residue reduction, unique quotient/nonzero-digit coordinates, and cardinality k^e + 1 of the canonical finite-level index. It proves unconditionally that this canonical family spans the complete kernel through level e, and proves exact rank k^e + 1 under the explicit hypothesis that the family is linearly independent. Lean does not prove that hypothesis or formalise Martin's positive-density theorem; the unconditional basis and rank theorem in the paper uses Martin externally.

claims.label: Residual-gauge obstruction for monomial minors
claims.statement: For a residual-weighted monomial matrix, common nonzero residual weights act by a right diagonal gauge and preserve determinant nonvanishing. Under the locked inverse-phase gauge, an exponent-one row is identically 1 even when the determinant remains nonzero; allowing row-dependent residuals reconstructs a consecutive-power matrix with zeroth row identically 1. Thus residual-blind rank, determinant, and conditioning criteria alone cannot exclude the target. This does not rule out a criterion with an additional arithmetic coupling identity, and it gives no irrationality criterion.

claims.label: Tempered tail-orbit rigidity criterion
claims.statement: For coefficients c(n) ≤ n, the binary series ∑ c(n)/2ⁿ is rational exactly when a tempered integer carry orbit exists, and every tempered orbit equals the scaled tail.

claims.label: Boolean–Möbius carry certificate equivalence
claims.statement: A nonempty normalised support, one omitting 0, with series value p/q exists exactly when a positive, square-root-bounded integer orbit with Boolean Möbius quotient exists; the support is reconstructed from the certificate.

claims.label: Rationality-forced reciprocal-mass lower bound
claims.statement: A rational support-series value with odd denominator part v forces reciprocal mass at least 1/ord_v(2), or divergence; an infinite support with dyadic-rational value has reciprocal mass divergent or greater than one.

claims.label: Carry states are unbounded over infinite rational-valued supports
claims.statement: An infinite support with rational series value has an unbounded positive carry state, closing finite-state readings of the carry system.

claims.label: Sublogarithmic divisor-coverage zero windows
claims.statement: A rational support-series value forces every zero window in the divisor-count coefficient to have length at most ε·log₂(N+1) + B, where B ≥ 0 is built from ε, c and v but is bound after the support and numerator, so no single constant is claimed uniform across supports. This constrains coverage; it does not solve universal #257.

claims.label: Greedy geometry of the Mersenne achievement set
claims.statement: The Mersenne achievement set is compact, perfect, totally disconnected, nowhere dense, and has Lebesgue measure one. Membership is equivalent to greedy survival at every level; for the target 1/2 it is exactly equivalent to the canonical greedy orbit omitting infinitely many exponents. No finite normalized support has value 1/2, so positive membership would automatically produce an infinite rational-valued support and refute universal #257. Finite exact-rational death certificates soundly prove non-membership (3/4 is excluded at level one). The strict-tail Cantor geometry is recorded by Kovač–Tao; no novelty claim is made for the formalised refinements.

claims.label: Exact band localization of the final skip between two takes
claims.statement: Suppose a take at rank b is followed by the next take at c > b+1, put q = 2^b − 1 and m = 2^(c−1), and write the pre-take residual as 1/R with 0 < R < q. The final intervening skip is dyadically unsafe exactly when q(m−1)/(q+m−1) < R < qm/(q+m), an interval of exact width q^2/((q+m)(q+m−1)). For one intervening skip this specializes to the two-thirds band (q(2q+1)/(3q+1), 2q(q+1)/(3q+2)), whose width is below 1/9; integral reciprocals never lie there, and the corresponding positive odd numerator is at least 7. These are local constraints: no theorem here says that the actual greedy orbit for 1/2 avoids a band or identifies the surviving last-producer cells with unsafe skips.

claims.label: Exact rational second-channel reduction for the target one half
claims.statement: A decidable rational separation predicate controls the greedy Mersenne orbit for the target 1/2. Lean verifies levels 1 through 6 exactly; proving the predicate for every n >= 7 would place 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set, equivalently would force infinitely many canonical greedy skips. The universal tail statement remains open.

claims.label: Campbell shift-synchronization strategy boundary
claims.statement: Campbell's application of the Alford-Granville-Pomerance estimate chooses delta = 1/4, so at prime-search height X the progression modulus d must satisfy d <= X^(1/4), equivalently d^4 <= X. In the proposed last-skip synchronization, P is the fatal-window prime cap, t the unavoidable phase period, and d the combined progression modulus. Taking X = P, the requirements 2 <= d, t <= d, P <= 4t, and d^4 <= P are inconsistent. The shifted-zero interface is guarded by a putative last skip and is exactly equivalent to infinitely many actual greedy skips and to membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. It is an endpoint restatement, not an independent Campbell input, and proves no half-membership.

claims.label: Transcendence of ∑ σ(m)/2^m
claims.statement: Nesterenko (1996); the ladder rung L(Id). Cited for positioning, not formalised here.

claims.label: Irrationality of the base-2 squarefree-support series
claims.statement: Duverney–Tachiya Corollary 1.2 and Example 1.1 prove linear independence of 1 and the squarefree Lambert sum including n=1; subtracting that rational term settles the support {n≥2:n squarefree} at base 2. Their condition |q|^L≤s does not cover the same support at integer bases b≥3. This result is not formalised here.

claims.label: Irrationality of the prime-support series ∑_p 1/(2^p − 1)
claims.statement: Tao–Teräväinen; settles the prime-support special case of #257. Only the identity bridge to ∑ ω(n)/2ⁿ is formalised, not the irrationality.

claims.label: Transport and curvature reductions for Erdős #249
claims.statement: Curvature, fixed-three exponent transport, anchored (3,5) transport, prime-jump, and balanced three-transport observables each have exact finite non-integrality consumers whose unbounded supply would imply irrationality of the totient constant. Every supply hypothesis remains open.

claims.label: Affine residue state and old-channel annihilation
claims.statement: The exact Möbius residue kernel has a periodic affine slope-and-intercept state. First-order exponent transport and every coefficient system with vanishing zeroth and first moments annihilate all divisor channels already present at the base height; a prime jump additionally has an explicit migrated-channel correction.

claims.label: Verified transport-window certificates
claims.bounded_domain: Exactly the prime-jump parameter triple (H,p,L)=(12,5,15) and the balanced three-transport pair (H,L)=(60,12).
claims.statement: Lean verifies the sharp prime-jump certificate at (H,p,L)=(12,5,15) and the balanced three-transport certificate at (H,L)=(60,12). These bounded instances do not establish any unbounded supply.

claims.label: First-harmonic gap implies a finite certificate
claims.statement: Under the explicit dyadic room inequality, a constant-saving first-harmonic bound on one block, or on any nonempty finite set of indices below its right endpoint, forces a certified non-integrality witness in that set. No cofinal harmonic estimate is asserted.

claims.label: Complex first-harmonic pivot decomposition
claims.statement: For each positive cofactor m at most sqrt(X)/2, the canonical supplier fibre is exactly the injective image of the primes p in the shifted product interval under N = mp - (L-s+1). This exact bijection does not make a supplier prime globally isolated: at X=16, L=20, s=1, m=2, N=18 the pivot is 38=2*19, while the same prime 19 divides the distinct window argument N+1=19. Removing the pivot phase gives an exact decomposition of the block first-harmonic sum into a centred supplier-fibre correlation, a supplier-fibre mean term, a bad-supplier term, and a non-supplier term. At a positive scale satisfying the explicit dyadic-room inequality, if the real part of the centred term is at most 14X/25 and the other three norms are at most X/100, X/100, and 8X/25, then the real first-harmonic sum is at most 9X/10 and yields a finite certificate. A cofinal supply of these budgets implies irrationality of S. No global supplier-prime isolation, prime-distribution estimate, or decorrelation estimate supplying the budgets is proved.

claims.label: Adjacent-pair phase separation reduction
claims.statement: At scales satisfying the explicit dyadic room inequality, a squared chordal separation of at least 19/25 between two adjacent first-harmonic phases in a dyadic block forces a certified non-integrality witness at one of the two indices. A cofinal supply of such adjacent pairs implies irrationality of the totient constant; no such supply is proved.

claims.label: Pivot anti-reconstruction and window-pair reduction
claims.statement: On a finite supplier fibre, sufficient counted phase-pair separation feeds a certified non-integrality witness through exact reconstruction-defect and variance identities. Cofinal pivot anti-reconstruction, reconstruction variance, or counted-pair producers imply irrationality of S. The fibre-free cofinal window-pair predicate is exactly equivalent to irrationality of S. No cofinal arithmetic producer is proved.

claims.label: Fixed-precision valuation-unit no-go theorem
claims.statement: At every fixed positive precision, every finite word of odd valuation-unit symbols admits a compatible carry orbit from an arbitrary incoming integer state, with each successive state within the corresponding valuation-unit radius. Thus bounded local signatures alone cannot exclude all finite centred endpoints; growing precision or global information remains necessary for an endpoint argument.

claims.label: LCM factor-ideal anchor-pulse no-go theorem
claims.statement: For every t ≥ 3, a nonzero synthetic affine carry has forcing letters in the principal ideal generated by φ(lcm(1,…,t)), matches every stated whole-ray anchor, and remains within the diagonal bounds while its state is a strict survivor. The same countermodel survives every finite integer shift polynomial. Thus factor ideals, whole-ray anchors, and finite-rank shift algebra alone do not force carry escape. The construction does not assert that its forcing letters are actual totient differences and does not rule out nonlinear use of fresh divisor channels.

claims.label: Actual LCM-orbit non-integrality frontier
claims.statement: Let H_a = lcm(1,…,2^a) and R_a = totientTail(2H_a) − totientTail(H_a). The totient series S is irrational if and only if, beyond every threshold a₀, some a ≥ a₀ has R_a ∉ ℤ. This is an exact cofinal non-integrality criterion for the actual LCM diagonal. That equivalence itself is not a quantitative separation estimate; the same source also provides a distinct sufficient route in which, cofinally in a₀, some a,q satisfy max 2 a₀ ≤ a, oddGuardedCanonicalAdjacentSuffixDepth (2^a) = 2q+1, and every integer z obeys 1/32 + actualLcmRawErrorRadius a q ≤ |actualLcmTailOrbit a − z|. This quantitative supply is not equivalent to the frontier criterion and remains unproved.

claims.label: Actual LCM positive corridor and top-edge boundary
claims.statement: For a ≥ 8 and J + (a + 6) < 2·2^a, the true translated LCM-orbit difference is strictly positive. If it is represented by an integer and the dyadic modulus has room for the directed endpoint strip, the carry survivor is strictly negative and the discrepancy residue is exactly the top-edge representative 2^K − carry_K, strictly between the strip’s lower edge and 2^K. Thus the positive corridor eliminates the nonnegative true survivor but does not itself produce a central-band contradiction; an independent arithmetic exclusion of the top boundary is still required.

claims.label: Tail-orbit phase-density and natural-prime strict-gap reductions
claims.statement: A uniform 11/100 nonpositive-phase density on arbitrarily late dyadic blocks yields an 89/100 first-harmonic saving and hence a finite certificate; alternatively, cofinally many natural prime indices with tail-orbit real part below 9/10 yield adaptive pivot escape. The exact initial phase is the scaled-angle character of (2^h - 1) times the series, and the tail phase follows a power-of-two squaring orbit from it; phase 1 is equivalent to an integral actual tail difference, while an entered dyadic root obstructs the strict-gap producer.

claims.label: Conditional terminal-scaled-vanishing half countermodel
claims.statement: Any HalfTerminalOnlyScaledVanishingSequence—finite words avoiding ranks 0 and 1, depths tending to infinity, and terminal carry divided by 2^M tending to zero—produces an infinite support A with ∑_{a∈A} 1/(2^a − 1) = 1/2. Hence that antecedent would refute universal Erdős #257, but it is not constructed here and does not itself settle half-membership.

claims.label: Conditional cofinal-cylinder half countermodel
claims.statement: If for every N there are M,K with max(N,1) ≤ M and a nonempty CylinderStage K M, then an infinite positive support A satisfies ∑_{a∈A} 1/(2^a − 1) = 1/2. This is a conditional countermodel frontier: the cofinal full-cylinder family is not constructed, so neither half-membership nor universal Erdős #257 is settled.

claims.label: Erdős #1049: irrationality of F(t) at rational bases
claims.statement: The universal rational-base irrationality assertion remains open in this release; checked exclusions at 3/2 and exact recurrence identities do not prove irrationality or rationality at a new endpoint.

claims.label: Base 3/2 coordinatewise corridor exclusion
claims.statement: With N ≥ 1 and K ≥ 1, the six-condition CoordinatewiseCorridor at base 3/2 is impossible for every natural Q and digit. This excludes only that literal coordinatewise clearing architecture, not rationality or irrationality of F(3/2) or any other proof architecture.

claims.label: Exact rational-base cleared-tail recurrence
claims.statement: For rational r, s, B, and F, a coefficient sequence coeff : ℕ → ℚ, and r ≠ 0, the denominator-cleared tail state satisfies rationalBaseClearedTailQ (r, s, B, F, coeff) (N + 1) = r · rationalBaseClearedTailQ (r, s, B, F, coeff) N − B · coeff (N + 1) · s^(N + 1) for every N. The identity is not derived from rationality and is not itself a rationality contradiction.

claims.label: Rational-base forcing-term growth boundary
claims.statement: For natural s, B, coeff, and N, if s ≥ 2, B ≥ 1, and coeff(N + 1) ≥ 1, then rationalBaseForcingNat s B coeff N ≥ 2^(N + 1); at s = 1 the same quantity is exactly B · coeff(N + 1). This is an elementary forcing-term bound, not a bounded-state contradiction or endpoint result.

claims.label: Van Assche q-Apéry diagonal recurrence non-transfer
claims.statement: For every real p > 1, the n = 0 residual obtained by applying the Amdeberhan–Zeilberger q-Apéry operator to Van Assche's moving diagonal is the displayed strictly negative factorisation, hence is nonzero. This rules out that selected diagonal for that recurrence at n = 0; it proves no general recurrence, endpoint, or #1049 irrationality result.

claims.label: Erdős #243: eventual Sylvester recurrence
claims.statement: The eventual Sylvester recurrence assertion remains open in this release; the bounded-rise barrier and conditional negative-part reductions leave the mixed-sign unbounded regime unresolved.

claims.label: Bounded-rise fresh-modulus coprimality barrier
claims.statement: For natural sequences u and m, if u tends to infinity with upward increments bounded by a fixed positive B, the moduli m are eventually greater than 1 and pairwise coprime, and each earlier m(i) is coprime to every later u(t), then the hypotheses are inconsistent. This is a reusable state-level obstruction, not a proof of the full Erdős #243 assertion.

claims.label: Eventually-periodic negative-orbit exclusion
claims.statement: For natural sequences a, D, C, and e with 2 ≤ a(n), positive e(N+n) < a(N+n), the exact recurrences D(n+1) = a(n)·D(n) and C(n+1) = C(n) + e(n), the shape equation D(n) + e(n) = (a(n)−1)·C(n), and a positive-period, positive-drift tail e(N+n+h) = e(N+n) and C(N+n+h) = C(N+n) + M with h > 0 and M > 0, the hypotheses are inconsistent. This is only the eventually-periodic negative-magnitude obstruction; mixed-sign and unbounded-negative behaviour remain outside the claim and the full Erdős #243 endpoint remains open.

claims.label: Cofinally bounded negative-magnitude exclusion
claims.statement: For natural sequences a, C, D, and magnitude and B > 0 satisfying 1 < a(n), C(n) > 0, C(n+1) + D(n) = a(n)·C(n), D(n+1) = a(n)·D(n), bounded rise C(n+1) ≤ C(n) + B, magnitude(n) > 0, division-free normalised vanishing (for every K, eventually K·magnitude(n) < C(n)), and a cofinal negative branch with 0 < e ≤ B and D(t) + e = (a(t)−1)·C(t), the hypotheses are inconsistent. This conditional no-go does not decide the full Erdős #243 endpoint or the mixed-sign and unbounded-negative regimes.

claims.label: Finite-support denominator period noncollapse
claims.statement: For every finite nonempty support F with 0 ∉ F and integer base b ≥ 2, the reduced denominator of the literal finite sum ∑_{n∈F} 1/(bⁿ−1) is coprime to b and the multiplicative order of b modulo that denominator equals F.lcm id. This finite-support theorem supplies no unbounded support certificate and does not settle the universal infinite-support Erdős #257 endpoint.

claims.label: Conditional exact rank of the all-base totient kernel
claims.statement: For integers k and e with 2 ≤ k and 1 ≤ e, if the explicit canonical all-base family is linearly independent over ℚ, then the span of the actual all-base totient kernel through level e has dimension k^e + 1. The linear-independence hypothesis is an external affine-ordering boundary; this coefficient-space result does not prove irrationality of the binary totient series.

claims.label: Erdős #249: irrationality of S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ
claims.statement: Not proved by this release. The reductions convert it into the unboundedness of the certificate supply, which is untouched.

claims.label: Erdős #257, universal form
claims.statement: Irrationality of ∑_{n∈A} 1/(2ⁿ − 1) for every infinite A is not proved by this release; only named families are formalised.

claims.label: Weighted-phase carry split and finite realised span for #269
claims.statement: The exact weighted-phase carry recurrence splits into a finite residue digit, each of the two coordinates staying inside its declared interval, and an integral quotient coboundary that is not controlled. An explicit factorisation through a finite-dimensional function-faithful observer then forces the realised symbolic span to be finite. Nothing here proves a finite-state quotient or a literal infinite realised span, and no rationality or irrationality conclusion follows.
